snippet.title: 🔴 LIVE: Celebrate 250 Years of America! | National Parks USA LIVESTREAM | National Geographic
snippet.description:
Celebrate the 250th Anniversary of the United States with a relaxing journey through America’s iconic National Parks. In this National Parks USA Livestream from National Geographic, explore five of America's most unique scenic landscapes and witness the animals that call these protected lands home. Whether enjoying as a relaxing nature background video or learning about the wildlife in the National Parks, this stream showcases the stunning natural beauty of the United States. 

Featured National Parks in this livestream:

Katmai (Alaska)
Explore Katmai, a land reborn from volcanic ash, and observe the vivid lives of bears, salmon, plovers and coastal wolves that call it home. 

Everglades (Florida)
As the first national park founded to protect wildlife and ecological richness, the Everglades teems with diverse life above and below water. 

Yellowstone (Wyoming/Montana/Idaho)
Discover a year in Yellowstone. Meet Wapiti wolves, bison and grizzly cubs, and marvel at the geysers and rich heritage of this trailblazing park.  

Olympic (Washington)
From glacial peaks to temperate rainforests and the rugged Pacific coast, Olympic National Park protects unique environments with rich biodiversity. 

Zion (Utah)
In Zion National Park, sandstone cliffs, slot canyons and the Virgin River converge, sculpting a vibrant landscape and refuge for wildlife to thrive.

snippet.title: 3 Mysterious Structures That Are Still Unexplained
snippet.description:
Some ancient structures raise a simple but unsettling question:

How were they built at all?

In this video we explore three astonishing ancient sites that continue to puzzle historians and researchers around the world.

First, we travel to southern India to see the Brihadeeswarar Temple, a thousand-year-old monument crowned by a granite block weighing around 80 tons, placed more than 60 meters above the ground.

Then we climb the remote summit of Mount Nemrut in Turkey, where enormous stone heads from a forgotten kingdom still stare across the mountains after more than 2,000 years.

Finally, we visit the mysterious Aramu Muru doorway near Lake Titicaca in Peru — a perfectly carved stone portal that appears to lead nowhere at all.

Across continents and centuries, these structures reveal something remarkable about the people who built them.

Their methods…
Their motivations…
And the knowledge that may have been lost to time.

Because sometimes the greatest mysteries of history are not myths or legends.

They are structures that still stand in front of us today.

---

snippet.description:
Thousands of protesters have marched in major South African cities this week, demanding that undocumented migrants leave the country. 
 
Demonstrators say illegal immigration is putting pressure on jobs, public services and contributing to crime, while critics warn the protests risk fuelling xenophobia and attacks on foreign nationals. 
 
President Cyril Ramaphosa has urged protesters to remain peaceful, while acknowledging the need for immigration reform.
 
Police say 25,000 migrants, most from other African countries, have been repatriated so far.

snippet.description:

In this 2+ hour Gordon Ramsay: Uncharted Mega Episode, Gordon travels from Louisiana's bayous to the Great Smoky Mountains and the rugged landscapes of Texas in search of authentic American cuisine, local ingredients, and unforgettable culinary traditions. He experiences a crawfish boil, rappels down a waterfall to fish for trout, and crafts his own spin on Texas barbecue. Featuring three, full episodes: 

Louisiana's Bayou Cuisine - 00:00 
When Chef Ramsay is told that “Cajun comes from the soul,” his soul searching takes him to South Louisiana’s swamps to test his skills and his luck.

The Great Smoky Mountains - 44:02 
Gordon rappels, kayaks, and forages his way through the Smoky Mountains in a hunt for some of the most unique ingredients the region has to offer. 

Texas Throwdown - 01:28:04
Chef Ramsay learns the meaning of “Texas Tough” as he herds cattle, catches a rattlesnake and hunts feral hog in the Lone Star State.

How do enormous figures appear with no clear method of construction? Why do entire cultures leave behind traces that end suddenly and violently, with no clear explanation? And why do certain sites continue to spark debate decades after their discovery, with no consensus in sight?

snippet.title: We Deciphered Ancient Text From 5000 Years Ago
snippet.description:
Irving Finkel lectures on Cuneiform, an ancient form of writing, dating all the way back to 5000 years ago. 

More than five thousand years ago, a revolutionary script emerged in the fertile lands of Mesopotamia that would transform how people counted, governed, worshipped and told stories. This was cuneiform, the world’s earliest known writing system.

In this episode of The Ancients, Tristan Hughes is joined by Dr Irving Finkel to uncover how cuneiform actually worked and how you would write it yourself. From humble beginnings as simple pictograms tracking beer and grain, to the wedge-shaped signs that recorded myths, laws and epic tales long before the Bible, this episode explores how cuneiform spread across Sumer, Babylon, Assyria and Persia — and why these clay tablets remain one of archaeology’s richest windows into the ancient world.

Check out the Ancients YouTube channel here: https://youtu.be/bSnPrL1sAdg

snippet.title: Ancient Egyptian Dog Mummy
snippet.description:
This mummified dog dates to around 3,400 years ago (New Kingdom, c. 1400 BC) and was discovered in Tomb KV50 in the Valley of the Kings, near the burial of Amenhotep II. The tomb contained both a dog and a baboon, suggesting it was part of a small group of animal burials linked to the royal court.  

The dog was carefully wrapped in linen, indicating it was treated with respect, possibly as a royal pet or companion animal rather than a mass-produced votive offering. Its proximity to the king’s tomb suggests a personal connection.

The video was animated with AI from original images of the dog mummy on display at the  Egyptian Museum in Cairo. #egypt #egyptian #ancientegypt #dogs #doglovers
